answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake, like basalt bedrock under a building: creating a new identity requires locking a real bond that is slashed on fraud, so spawning thousands of fakes becomes expensive. Each agent becomes a vertex in a reputation graph, with trust flowing only through verified interactions, so fake clusters sit isolated on a ledge with no incoming trust and earn nothing. Honest agents accumulate attested history; sybils cannot fake that graph.
